\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item Break test as elsewhere: regression-based Chow sweep, 15\% trim, 10,000-draw permutation
null, seed 42. \textbf{None of these measures returns a trend, and none returns a break that
survives its own confidence interval.} They are reported here rather than as figure panels because
a null should not occupy a figure, and because their agreement is informative in itself: the
absence of a trend in year-on-year change is not an artefact of the index chosen.
\item \textbf{Kullback--Leibler should not be used on the agenda series.} Twenty-three per cent of
topic-year cells are empty, so KL is undefined without a smoothing constant, and with one applied
the forward and reverse divergences correlate $r=-0.066$ --- the direction of comparison, which is
arbitrary, decides the answer. Public spending has no empty cells, KL is well defined, and the two
directions correlate $r=+0.985$. Jensen--Shannon is symmetric and defined in the presence of zeros,
and is the only member of the family valid on both series.
\item \textbf{Units.} Pedersen churn is in percentage points; divergence measures are in bits.
\item \textbf{What is not null} is reported in the figures: the government agenda broadens across
the period while public spending concentrates, both at $p<0.001$. In neither case is the date of
the change identifiable.
\end{tablenotes}
